problem: Filesystem publication under the authority mutex stalls unrelated foreground commits.
decision: Reserve the existing physical publication lane, publish using owned handles outside authority, then reconcile successor sequence/hash/entity root. History compaction also prepares payload routes outside authority.

limits: The 100 ms CONTROL fsync pause is deliberately injected around a real file operation; it establishes isolation, not usual-volume latency.
Two ABBA runs per arm are finite observations; 128-case tails overlap and do not establish a universal latency win.
The 1000-conversation cohort still exceeds its 1-second streaming P99 budget.
Real provider/browser latency and sustained soak are not measured.
No backend, durability tier, retry policy or publication acknowledgement policy changes.
No uniform RSS reduction is established.
operational_bounds: One existing driver and one reserved publication; no new resident worker, queue, persistent format or admission bound. Frozen manifest bytes live until publication completion; pre-existing predecessor/successor WAL ceilings remain.

live_rollout.difference_from_measured_source: Only build.rs adds existing Linux embedded-mimalloc NODELETE linker protection; all Rust source bodies match the tested candidate.

embedded_process_recovery.timing_scope: Embedded open and client health only; excludes process launch and replay comparison. No latency verdict.
embedded_process_recovery.scope: Exact acknowledged running/final Turn documents, text and event rows including timestamps. Real embedded process kill/reap/reopen. No performance verdict; original abandon benchmark coverage remains incomplete.

live_rollout.scope: Single supervised native-child activation after official artifact/pin deployment. Application PID unchanged. Online WAL growth is write progress, not a per-user write-latency distribution. Warm online read timings overlap; no live read-speedup claim.
